name: flat-bool-debug-color
rationale: The generated companion supplies the flat boolean varying; the fragment selects its declared grayscale half value with alpha one, captured byte-exactly.

name: gathers-and-nearest-samples-of-denormal-32-bit-float-texels
rationale: Plain gathers and nearest samples of 32-bit float textures whose texels are mostly denormals of both signs: Metal's sample and gather hand a denormal texel back as it is, where a device's may read it as zero (RADV, NVIDIA, ANV). Texture 0 is an r32_float 8x8, texture 1 an rgba32_float 8x8, texture 2 an r32_float 8x8 2D array of 2 layers; every texel is a denormal (three in four) or a signed zero, a smallest normal or an ordinary value. Lane i reads at buffer 0's float4 i's xy, through a nearest clamp-to-edge sampler and a nearest repeating sampler without a mip filter, and writes eight float4s from out[8i] (buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB): texture 0's gather (edge), its nearest sample (edge), texture 1's gather of y (edge) and of w (repeat), its nearest sample (edge), texture 0's gather (repeat), texture 1's nearest sample at offset (1, -1) (repeat), and texture 2's layer-1 nearest sample (edge). Lanes: one per texel at its centre, corner or a quarter between, and eight outside or at the edges of [0, 1]. The AIR has no loop.

name: gated-bias-off
rationale: Five air.* symbols the corpus reaches once or four times each and that no authored case covered: air.fast_acosh.f32, air.fast_asinh.f32, air.fast_atanh.f32, air.fast_tan.v3f32 and air.normalize_function_constant_predicate.i16. The fixture keeps the default fast-math compile, because that is what emits the four fast_ symbols, so every call carries LLVM's fast flags. MSL 8.1 leaves an infinite or NaN operand or result undefined under fast math, and under nsz either zero is a correct result. MSL Table 8.2 defines the fast acosh, asinh and atanh by log formulas and the fast tan as sin * (1 / cos), with log and sin bounded, so what they answer is a reading of Apple's approximation inside that bound, never a pinned value. The rows ask each function only at the argument where its value is zero: acosh(1) in rows 0 and 1, asinh(+0) in rows 2 to 4, atanh(+0) in rows 5 to 8, and tan(+0) on all three lanes of the float3 in rows 9 to 11. Even there the zero is a bounded reading, not a pinned answer: at these arguments the formulas reduce to log(1), whose fast error is at most 2^-21 absolute on [0.5, 2] (asinh(+0) through the fast sqrt(1) = 1 * rsqrt(1), within 2 ulp, and atanh(+0) through the fast division 1 / 1), and to sin(+0), at most 2^-13 absolute, so a small non-zero result would conform, and under nsz so would -0. Metal answers +0 in every one of those rows. The translation's GLSL.std.450 Acosh, Asinh, Atanh and Tan inherit Vulkan's 2^-21 (Log) and 2^-11 (Sin) absolute bounds, so these rows match only on a device that, like Metal, answers exactly +0, and the byte comparison reports any other conforming answer. The case's first version also asked acosh(+inf), asinh(-0), asinh(-inf), atanh(-0), atanh(+1), atanh(-1), tan(-0) and tan(2^-20). The first seven are undefined under these flags: Metal answered asinh(-inf) with NaN, its log formula at -inf, and lavapipe answered -inf. tan(2^-20) is bounded, not pinned. has_bias is a short function constant that gates the bias argument, which is the spelling that makes Metal emit air.normalize_function_constant_predicate.i16 into air.static_init; the last row is 3.25 plus the bias when it is bound, an exact sum. This case sets has_bias to 0, so the bias argument is not bound at all and the last row is the unmodified input, 3.25.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-seven-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 27 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-six linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: cull-every-ray-that-reaches-the-only-triangle
rationale: Every ray leaves one origin below the plane of the only triangle, so every ray that reaches it sees the same face. Culling that face is therefore the whole difference between some rays hitting and none: with none hitting, the kernel's occlusion numerator is a sum of 127 zeros and the stored ratio is exactly 0, whatever the hemisphere-sampling transcendentals did to the ray directions.

name: cull-the-face-no-ray-reaches-and-hit-them-all
rationale: The companion of the front-cull case: the same scene with back-face culling, which culls nothing because every ray reaches the triangle's front. It fixes the un-culled answer, so it fails if a cull mode is applied to the wrong face or to a face the mode does not name.

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The chirp input is an explicit zero-filled bounded buffer.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-three-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 and 3 and receives exact float4 zero from both linked _uber_clear bodies. A five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected as the result. This entry writes the complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0), which the poisoned 4x1 resource captures byte-exactly.

name: float-denormals-in-vector-arithmetic-comparisons-and-functions-under-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads the float vectors (a, b, c) and the int vector n from in[4i .. 4i + 3] and writes 64 words, each row lane-wise: a + b, a - b, a * b, fma(a, b, c), a * b + c, the six comparisons of a and b as bits (<, <=, ==, !=, >, >= at bits 0 to 5), floor(a), ceil(a), sqrt(a), rsqrt(a), ldexp(a, n), (a * b) * c, float(n) * a - c, the comparisons a * b < c, -a < b and fabs(a) == b as bits 0 to 2, fmin(a, b) * c, and step(a, b). Over the 1024 lanes, (a, b) is every pair of a 32-value pool: both zeros, denormals of both signs (the smallest, the largest, others), the smallest normals and their neighbours, values whose products or differences land among the denormals (2^-64, 2^-63, 2^-70, 2^-100, 2^-30, 2^30), and ordinary values; c is the pool at another stride and n runs over -126 to 127. It measures how Metal reads a float denormal operand and flushes a denormal result in vector arithmetic, comparisons, ldexp, sqrt, rsqrt, floor and ceil, and in an operation whose operand is another operation's result. Compiled with the default fast math: the calls are the fast_ ones and the arithmetic carries every flag, so a * b + c is a contracted pair.

name: one-d-array-reads-and-width-queries-at-32-and-16-bit-coordinates
rationale: air.read_texture_1d_array and air.get_width_texture_1d_array, decoded by the AIR front end: lane i reads texel (i mod 5, (i / 5) mod 3) of three 1D texture arrays -- texture 0 rgba32_float 5 wide x 3 slices (normal floats over many binades, either sign) through a read texture at 32-bit coordinates, texture 1 rgba32_uint 6 x 4 (random words) at 16-bit coordinates, texture 2 rgba16_float 7 x 3 (finite halves over every binade, subnormals included) through a sampled texture's read -- and writes the three texels' words (the half one widened to float) to out[4i .. 4i + 2] and the three widths (5, 6, 7) and texture 0's array size (3) to out[4i + 3] of buffer 0 (uint4 elements), pre-filled with 0xAB. 32 lanes, so every texel of texture 0's extent is read at least twice; every coordinate is inside every texture. The AIR has no loop.

name: one-d-array-reads-and-width-queries-with-normal-halves
rationale: air.read_texture_1d_array and air.get_width_texture_1d_array, decoded by the AIR front end, with every half texel normal: lane i reads texel (i mod 5, (i / 5) mod 3) of three 1D texture arrays -- texture 0 rgba32_float 5 wide x 3 slices (normal floats over many binades, either sign) through a read texture at 32-bit coordinates, texture 1 rgba32_uint 6 x 4 (random words) at 16-bit coordinates, texture 2 rgba16_float 7 x 3 (normal halves over every binade, either sign) through a sampled texture's read -- and writes the three texels' words (the half one widened to float) to out[4i .. 4i + 2] and the three widths (5, 6, 7) and texture 0's array size (3) to out[4i + 3] of buffer 0 (uint4 elements), pre-filled with 0xAB. 32 lanes, so every texel of texture 0's extent is read at least twice; every coordinate is inside every texture. The sibling case with subnormal halves records the candidate's half denormal flush (F16DenormFlush); this one keeps the 1D-array addressing exact. The AIR has no loop.

name: four-tap-half-fma-chain-lands-on-four-texel-centres
rationale: A four-tap blur whose taps accumulate through air.fma.v4f16. The render target is one texel, so the harness-fixed varying is (0.5,0.5), and the four authored offsets move it to 0.125, 0.375, 0.625 and 0.875 -- exactly the texel centres of a 4x4 source. Each tap therefore reads one distinct texel, (0,0), (2,1), (1,3) and (3,2), and the other twelve texels hold different values, so a tap that landed on the wrong texel or paired with the wrong weight changes the answer. The coordinates are texel centres, so the case does not depend on the sampler's filter either. Every texel channel and every weight is a small power-of-two multiple, so each product and each running sum is exactly representable in half: fusing or not fusing the multiply-add gives the same bits, which is the one freedom an FMA lowering has. The accumulator is (-2.875, 1.71875, 4.5625, 1.25) and the edr scale of 0.5 halves only rgb, leaving alpha at 1.25.

name: irreducible-pointer-phi-rebuild-observed-at-arm-0
rationale:
One of three cases on one fixture. `remat_phi`'s non-invariant fold in `src/native/relooper.rs` -- load the phi's tag, then rebuild the pointer as `select(tag == i, arm_i, ...)` -- fires on exactly 6 of the 14,579 corpus sources, only 2 of which translate OK, and the smaller of those two is 58 KB. No authored case reached it. `kernel_irreducible_three_way.ll` does not either: its three pointer arms are constant offsets off one base, so the address collapses upstream to a spilled index and the fold never runs.

Three DIFFERENT bindings defeat that collapse -- there is no common base to factor out -- and the disassembly confirms it with two `OpSelect %_ptr_PhysicalStorageBuffer_uint`, which is the fold itself. Because a case observes one buffer, the arm mapping is read by three cases over the same dispatch; this one observes out0 (the `v*3` arm).

Of the 32 threads, 11 take this arm and write their value; the other 21 must leave the 0xa0a0a0a0 fill untouched. So each case checks the mapping in BOTH directions: a fold that selected the wrong arm either drops a value that should be here or deposits one that should not be, and the three cases together pin all three tag values. A scalar-only case cannot see this at all -- the numbers would all still be right, just stored through the wrong pointer.

Metal runs the sibling `.metal`, the same automaton with one entry and a ternary picking the destination. Both spellings were simulated independently over all 32 inputs before authoring, and Metal's own output is byte-for-byte the sequence derived from the irreducible form. `input[tid] = tid`, so n runs 0..31: every switch case at entry, every exit arm, and trip counts 1 through 31.

name: color-of-a-pixel-rate-fragment-only-where-its-stencil-passes
rationale: A per-pixel [[stencil]] output (word x of buffer 0: ['0x22', '0x23', '0x122', '0x0']) beside a color output (word x of buffer 1) to an R32Uint target of 4 samples per pixel initialised to 0xAAAA0000 + 4x + s: a sample whose stencil test fails keeps its color. (Metal's [[stencil]] semantics as measured on the reference device, 4x included): the output's low 8 bits r are the reference of both faces; each covered sample's test is (r & readMask) cmp (s & readMask) for its stored s; the face's operation writes (s & ~writeMask) | (op(s, r) & writeMask); a sample that fails the stencil test gets no depth or color; the stencil test precedes the depth test. The pass is multisampled, 4 samples per pixel, and the draw is the executors' fullscreen triangle (1 instance), which covers every sample and is back-facing under the default clockwise winding (case 8db41494), over a 4x1 stencil attachment whose every sample holds 0x22 (a multisampled stencil is authored uniform and cleared to it). The back face's state: compare equal, stencil failure keep, depth failure increment_clamp, pass increment_clamp, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF; the front face's (compare always, stencil failure zero, depth failure zero, pass zero, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF) would give other values. The encoder's references are 0 and unused. Predicted color, pixel by pixel, 4 samples each: ['0x11111111', '0x11111111', '0x11111111', '0x11111111', '0xaaaa0004', '0xaaaa0005', '0xaaaa0006', '0xaaaa0007', '0x33333333', '0x33333333', '0x33333333', '0x33333333', '0xaaaa000c', '0xaaaa000d', '0xaaaa000e', '0xaaaa000f']. On a device without VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export the engine tests and writes each sample in the shader under the ordered pixel interlock against a multisampled shadow of the attachment, keeping the passing samples in its sample mask. The observation is every sample of the whole render target attachment, pixel by pixel, sample by sample. The AIR has no loop.

name: stencil-output-at-sample-rate-references-in-primitive-order
rationale: Three overlapping fragments per sample in a pass of 4 samples ([[sample_id]]): each sample's fragment counts the fragments of its sample before it in raster order group 0 (buffer 2, one word per sample) and takes that word of its sample's run of buffer 0 (runs ['[0x10, 0x20, 0x05]', '[0x90, 0x7F, 0x7F]', '[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]', '[0x00, 0x00, 0x00]', '[0x7F, 0x7E, 0x7D]', '[0x80, 0x80, 0x80]', '[0xFF, 0x01, 0x00]', '[0x40, 0x41, 0x40]']), so the earlier instance's fragment takes the earlier word if the group orders them as Metal orders each sample's stencil tests, in primitive order. Each test reads the previous fragment's write to its sample. (Metal's [[stencil]] semantics as measured on the reference device, 4x included): the output's low 8 bits r are the reference of both faces; each covered sample's test is (r & readMask) cmp (s & readMask) for its stored s; the face's operation writes (s & ~writeMask) | (op(s, r) & writeMask); a sample that fails the stencil test gets no depth or color; the stencil test precedes the depth test. The pass is multisampled, 4 samples per pixel, and the draw is the executors' fullscreen triangle (3 instances), which covers every sample and is back-facing under the default clockwise winding (case 8db41494), over a 2x1 stencil attachment whose every sample holds 0x80 (a multisampled stencil is authored uniform and cleared to it). The back face's state: compare less, stencil failure increment_clamp, depth failure replace, pass replace, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF; the front face's (compare always, stencil failure zero, depth failure zero, pass zero, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF) would give other values. The encoder's references are 0 and unused. Predicted stencil, pixel by pixel, 4 samples each: [0x05, 0x80, 0x83, 0x00, 0x7D, 0x81, 0x00, 0x40]. On a device without VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export the engine tests and writes each sample in the shader under the ordered pixel interlock against a multisampled shadow of the attachment, keeping the passing samples in its sample mask. The observation is every sample of the whole stencil attachment, pixel by pixel, sample by sample. The AIR has no loop.

The back face's state: compare greater, stencil failure zero, depth failure replace, pass replace, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF; the front face's (compare always, stencil failure zero, depth failure zero, pass zero, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF) would give other values. The encoder's references are 0 and unused. Predicted stencil, pixel by pixel, 4 samples each: [0x41, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80, 0x7F]. On a device without VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export the engine tests and writes each sample in the shader under the ordered pixel interlock against a multisampled shadow of the attachment, keeping the passing samples in its sample mask. The observation is every sample of the whole stencil attachment, pixel by pixel, sample by sample. The AIR has no loop.

name: stencil-output-at-sample-rate-under-read-and-write-masks
rationale: A per-sample [[stencil]] output ([[sample_id]]; sample s of pixel x returns word 2x + s of buffer 0: ['0x45', '0x46', '0x5', '0x9c', '0x2f5', '0x15', '0x0', '0xff']) in a pass of 2 samples, compared through read mask 0x0F and written through write mask 0xF0. (Metal's [[stencil]] semantics as measured on the reference device, 4x included): the output's low 8 bits r are the reference of both faces; each covered sample's test is (r & readMask) cmp (s & readMask) for its stored s; the face's operation writes (s & ~writeMask) | (op(s, r) & writeMask); a sample that fails the stencil test gets no depth or color; the stencil test precedes the depth test. The pass is multisampled, 2 samples per pixel, and the draw is the executors' fullscreen triangle (1 instance), which covers every sample and is back-facing under the default clockwise winding (case 8db41494), over a 4x1 stencil attachment whose every sample holds 0x35 (a multisampled stencil is authored uniform and cleared to it). The back face's state: compare equal, stencil failure invert, depth failure replace, pass replace, read mask 0x0F, write mask 0xF0; the front face's (compare always, stencil failure zero, depth failure zero, pass zero, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF) would give other values. The encoder's references are 0 and unused. Predicted stencil, pixel by pixel, 2 samples each: [0x45, 0xC5, 0x05, 0xC5, 0xF5, 0x15, 0xC5, 0xC5]. On a device without VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export the engine tests and writes each sample in the shader under the ordered pixel interlock against a multisampled shadow of the attachment, keeping the passing samples in its sample mask. The observation is every sample of the whole stencil attachment, pixel by pixel, sample by sample. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-three
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 23 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-two linked _uber_clear bodies. name: dsm2-shuffle-past-the-thread-count-eight
rationale: A threadgroup of 8, lanes 8-31 absent; every simd_shuffle_down and simd_shuffle_xor, and the even lanes' simd_shuffle, read absent lanes. Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. Every thread writes all three words. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm2-shuffle-past-the-thread-count-forty-eight
rationale: A threadgroup of 48: simdgroup 0 is whole (every word defined), simdgroup 1 has lanes 0-15 only. Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. name: dsm2-shuffle-past-the-thread-count-sixteen
rationale: A threadgroup of 16, lanes 16-31 absent. The even lanes' simd_shuffle reads lanes 16-31, lanes 8-15's simd_shuffle_down reads lanes 16-23, and every lane's simd_shuffle_xor reads lanes 16-31: Metal leaves those values undefined, and these words are its answer (the caller's value, zero, another lane's, or nondeterministic across the qualification's three runs). The odd lanes' simd_shuffle and lanes 0-7's simd_shuffle_down read existing lanes. Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. Every thread writes all three words. The AIR has no loop.

Inputs (B): in[g] = 0x3C000000 + 0x00020203 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. Every thread writes all three words. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm2-shuffle-past-the-thread-count-two-threadgroups
rationale: Two threadgroups of 16: whether an absent lane's word depends on the threadgroup (or reads the other threadgroup's threads). Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. Every thread writes all three words. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm2-shuffle-whole-simdgroup
rationale: The control: a threadgroup of 32, every source lane exists, so every word is defined: out[3g] = in[src[L]], out[3g + 1] = in[g + 8] for L < 24 and in[g] otherwise (Metal keeps the caller's value past the simdgroup), out[3g + 2] = in[g ^ 16]. Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the delta src[32] = 8, and the mask src[33] = 16. out[3g] is lane g's simd_shuffle, out[3g + 1] its simd_shuffle_down, out[3g + 2] its simd_shuffle_xor. Every thread writes all three words. The AIR has no loop.

name: read-an-element-of-a-texture-array-at-a-dynamic-index
rationale: Eight threads read texel (g >> 2, 0) of element g & 3 of a four-element array<texture2d<float>, 4> bound at texture 0 (access.handle.array_load.clamped: the dynamic index into the sized handle array is clamped under isolation). Element e is a 2x1 rgba32_float texture whose texel x is (10e + x, e, x, 1.5), so out[g] = (10 (g & 3) + (g >> 2), g & 3, g >> 2, 1.5). Every index is in range. The AIR has no loop.

name: vote-and-ballot-three-masks-over-one-thirty-two-lane-simdgroup
rationale: An owned fixture for the subgroup vote and ballot families: air.simd_any (2 corpus sources), air.simd_all (1) and air.simd_broadcast_first (3) had no authored case, and air.simd_ballot.i64 (6) and air.simd_is_first (30) are here because they read the same lane model. Every answer is a function of thread_index_in_simdgroup and every thread stores at the slot its own lane names, so nothing in the expected bytes depends on which thread received which lane. The predicate is bit `lane` of a mask read from buffer 1, which makes simd_ballot's answer the mask itself: bits indexed by the physical subgroup lane rather than by simd_lane_id come back rotated, and a vote taken over a subgroup wider than the simdgroup mixes in lanes this 32-thread dispatch never asked about. Three masks separate the two votes from each other and from the ballot: 0xA5A5A5A5 alternates, so any is true and all is false; 0xFFFFFFFF makes both true; 0 makes both false -- a lowering that answered `all` as `the ballot is non-zero`, or `any` as `the ballot equals the active mask`, agrees with exactly one of the three. The two stored high halves must be zero on a 32-lane simdgroup, so a 64-bit mask that carried a neighbouring simdgroup's lanes shows up there and nowhere else. simd_broadcast_first is given lane + 100, which differs in every lane, so its answer names the lane it chose: 100 is lane 0 and nothing else is. The buffer is sixteen bytes longer than the 32 x 8 words the kernel writes, and those bytes must still hold their 0x9E poison.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: eight-lanes-one-pass-k4-of-66-scatter-zeros
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-width case, whose K = 0 and srcWidth = 0 skip every read and write. Here MPSTopKParameters (binding 29) holds K = 4, srcWidth = 66; kMPSUserConstant = 2 gives 1 pass (kKU4O4 = 1), and kMPSNDArrayFunctionConstant = 0 clears accumulationOption, so writes go to postfixPrimary_f. 8 threads along y in one threadgroup. The first pass reads the row through prefixPrimary_4xf (retained module returns zeroinitializer) for columns 0 to 63 and prefixPrimary_f (retained writer returns 1.0) for columns 64 to 65, and zero-fills as it reads: the 4-wide part through the no-op postfixPrimary_4xf, the tail through postfixPrimary_f with 0.0. The selection is the forward kernel's (strict ogt to enter, strict olt to reorder, the partner's entry wins merge ties, later passes exclude earlier indices), so thread 0 selects columns [65, 64, 28, 29] and scatters the gradient read through prefixSecondary_f (retained module returns 0.0) to each. Every write stores +0.0, so the observed words are +0.0 on the tail and the selected columns and the 0xab fill elsewhere, which pins the AIR's own deterministic tie rule (barrier-separated exchanges with fixed partners, no atomics); writes that meet on a column store the same +0.0, so order does not matter. A single pass leaves no later merge to race the index broadcast. srcWidth bounds the read loops, log2 of the lane count the merge rounds, 4 the insertion and scatter loops.

name: linked-zero-width-topkv-grad
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The zero TopK parameters set srcWidth and K to zero. Every unconditionally selected top-4 helper exits on its initial four-elements-greater-than-srcWidth check before prefix linkage, while K zero prevents postfix destination writes, leaving the bounded device-array output unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: sample-each-of-three-textures-through-one-dynamic-array-index
rationale:
A dynamically indexed `metal::array` of three SAMPLED textures read through one sampler -- the half of `native/opaque_image_select.rs` that no authored case reached. Logical SPIR-V has no pointer-to-image, so the emitter cannot name the handle the index picks; it collects the whole store set into the alloca, replays it as a select tree over the three image ids, and proves every arm is available at the sample site. A sampled image is a different SPIR-V value from a directly read one (`OpSampledImage`, not `OpImage`) and needs its own image-type recovery, which is why the file has two halves. The corpus has exactly one host for this half, an 870-line tone mapper; a twenty-line fixture reaches the same rules.

Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source: 18 functions no cased source reaches, being `plan_tree`, `replay_selected_image`, `sampled_image_image_type`, `is_sampled_image_value_op`, `tree_values_available_at` and `value_available_at` with their closures, plus `collect_select_tree`, `fresh` and `tir::operands::extract_aggregate_member`.

All three arms are live in one dispatch of three threads. `which` is (2, 0, 1) rather than the identity, so a select tree wired in the wrong order answers differently instead of agreeing by accident; `% 3` keeps the index in range without letting the frontend fold it, because the value comes from a buffer.

The comparison is exact. Texture k's texel (x, y) carries the four channels 100(k+1) + 10(2y + x) + c for c in 1..4, and the shader folds them as r + 10g + 100b + 1000a. The sampler is `nearest`, `clamp_to_edge` and normalized, so (0.25, 0.75) on a 2x2 image resolves to texel (0, 1) with no filtering at all: 0.25 * 2 = 0.5 and 0.75 * 2 = 1.5 each land strictly inside their own texel, neither on a boundary, so no rounding rule is being relied on. Every term and every partial sum is an integer below 2^24, exactly representable in binary32, so the `fast` reassociation the frontend is free to apply cannot move the result. The three answers are 359841, 137641 and 248741: the texture index sets the hundred-thousands digit and the texel index sets the tens, so a wrong image and a wrong texel are separately visible, and the output buffer is pre-filled with -1.0, which no arm can produce. Metal answered exactly those three floats, derived in advance, and MoltenVK Matches.

name: linked-k299-vector-matrix-per-tensor-asymmetric-half
rationale: Reaching variant of 905b2e84 (linked-zero-shape-vector-matrix-per-tensor-half), whose zero shape and constants leave the kernel no work. It is the float variant f53027fb on this half-activation kernel of the same template: the same constants (the simdgroup-per-row path without matrix multiply-accumulate, one K split, a 128-element K tile, four simdgroups per threadgroup, two activation vectors, the partial-reduction tail on and kDiv4 off, asymmetric per-tensor A, the direct pD write), the same params and the same int8 A[r][k] = (5k + 3r) mod 7 - 3 (ARowBytes 300), over half B[x][k] = (3k + 2x) mod 5 - 2 (BRowBytes 600: rows of 300 halves). Two threadgroups of 128 lanes (grid 128x2) give rows tgid.y*4 + simdgroup, 0 to 7: rows 0 to 6 are below N = 7 and row 7 returns at the bound. Each row reduces K = 299 in float (each half B converted exactly): two 128-element main steps, the guarded tail to K4 = 296, then lane 0's 3-element remainder, each subtracting the zero point 1 read as int8 from table entry 1; simd_sum, times the scale 0.5 read as half from table entry 0, and lane 0 writes half pD[x*8 + r] (DRowBytes 16: rows of 8 halves). Every product (a - 1) * b is an integer of magnitude at most 8 and every partial sum an integer below 2400, so each sum is exact in float in any order, and each result, a multiple of 0.5 of magnitude below 1024, is exact in half. The 32 observed bytes are pD's 16 halves: 14 written once each by a single lane, halves 7 and 15 keeping the 0xab fill (row 7 writes nothing). Every loop is finite by these inputs: K = 299 bounds the reduction, N = 7 the rows, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: linked-zero-shape-vector-matrix-per-tensor-half
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: All matrix dimensions, tile controls, and optional feature predicates are authored as zero. The sole bounded invocation therefore has no output work and leaves the poisoned half destination unchanged while retaining the exact postfix linkage contract. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: tessellate-one-triangle-behind-eleven-bytes-of-padding
rationale: Device ground truth for the packed-struct layout this kernel's parameter buffer depends on. `screeenspace_adaptive_parameters_t` is `<{ i32, i8, [11 x i8], CFXDeformerTransforms, float, [12 x i8] }>`, and its own air.struct_type_info node puts `ndcTessellationFactor` at offset 208 -- behind an eleven-byte pad that starts at 5, which only lands there if an array keeps its element's alignment. Every tessellation factor this case reads back is that float times an edge length, so a layout that moved it reads different bytes and answers differently. Both matrices the kernel uses are the identity, which makes the model-view transform carry the three positions through unchanged and collapses the projection's denominator to exactly 1: the column it multiplies the edge length by is 1 and its three w terms are 0, so the perspective divide is by one whatever the midpoint is. The triangle is (0,0,0), (3,4,0) and (0,0,12), whose three edges are the 3-4-5, 5-12-13 and axis-aligned lengths 5, 13 and 12 -- every squared length an exact small integer, so the dot products are exact under any fast-math association and the only inexact step is the square root of a perfect square. Times an ndcTessellationFactor of 0.5 that is 2.5, 6.5 and 6.0, each exactly representable in half and more than a hundred half-ULPs from its neighbours, so a fast square root that is a few float ULPs off still truncates to the same three halves. Only the first six bytes are compared: the kernel writes lanes 0, 1 and 2 of the half4 and leaves lane 3 undefined.

name: nan-model-vector-float-half-conversions-of-nan-operands
rationale: Which NaN Metal's vector conversions between float and half (air.convert) answer, beside the scalar casts (compiled without fast math): lane i reads a float4 a and a half4 h and writes half4(a) (two words), half(a.x) | half(a.y) << 16 (the scalar fptrunc), float(h.x) (the scalar fpext), and float4(h) (four words). Values: every float NaN kind (quiet and signaling of either sign, payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3fe000, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff), the narrowing's range and rounding edges (+-65504, 65519.996, +-65520, 2^-24, 2^-25, 3 * 2^-26, 2^-14, a float denormal, 1e30) and controls; every half NaN kind (payloads 0, 1, 2, 0xaa, 0x155, 0x1fe, 0x1ff), the infinities, +-65504, subnormals and controls; each value in every vector lane. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected.
